source.title: Revisiting Robustness for LLM Safety Alignment via Selective Geometry Control
source.authors: Yong-Hui Yang; Wen Tao; Jilong Liu; Xing-Yu Zhu; Junfeng Fang; Weibiao Huang; Le Wu; Richang Hong; Tat-Seng Chua

record.file_problem: Some extracted figure labels and table layouts are garbled or flattened, but the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether safety-relevant behavior is concentrated in a small parameter subset using probe-selected neurons and selective-versus-uniform/random geometry control, a different method from the claim's original fine-tuning and token-position measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure few-example harmful or benign fine-tuning, per-token KL across response positions, compliant-prefix or suffix bypasses, or safety depth across response tokens. Main ShaPO benchmark comparisons report the method's performance but do not isolate parameter localization; Table 3 and Figure 5 directly compare geometry-control selection or subset size. Figure 1 measures concentration of worst-case alignment-loss increase, not harmful-response behavior, so it is recorded under none.
record.test_reason: The paper takes safety localization (citing Wei et al. 2024 and Zhao et al. 2025b) as the premise for its ShaPO training method. Its results report only that method's performance. Table 3 and Figure 5 are ablations of where sharpness-aware perturbation is applied during DPO. They do not test whether a small parameter set carries safety behaviour, for example by removing or altering those weights and measuring refusal. Figure 1 measures how much worst-case alignment-loss increase comes from a few probe-selected neurons. That is a loss-sensitivity construct, not a rate of harmful compliance. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that selective geometry control on probe-identified alignment-critical parameters improves safety robustness under domain shift and noisy supervision. They say it avoids the over-regularization of uniform control and composes with data-centric robust methods.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains preference-aligned models using a sharpness-aware objective with perturbations restricted to probe-selected parameter directions. It does not apply the harmful/benign few-example fine-tuning intervention or measure response-position KL or token-opening bypasses.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies by geometry-control strategy, IID versus OOD evaluation, judge, and selected-neuron ratio. The Table 3 control comparison is on LLaMA-3-8B; the text reports the Top-1% ratio as the OOD ASR minimum.

fits_no_version.finding: Perturbing fewer than 0.5% of probe-selected value-vector neurons accounts for over 80% of worst-case alignment-loss increase in LLaMA-3-8B, versus substantially less for random neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Worst-case DPO alignment-loss sensitivity concentrates in a small probe-identified neuron subset.

fits_no_version.finding: Restricting SAM perturbations to the top-1% probe-selected neurons gives slightly lower OOD ASR than random or uniform SAM in DPO training on LLaMA-3-8B (MD 26.31% vs 28.56%/26.83%; NV 14.12% vs 16.87%/15.12%). IID ASR is comparable across strategies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness regularization targeted at safety-probe-aligned neurons improves OOD safety generalization of preference-aligned models more than untargeted regularization.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The direct control comparison in Table 3 is reported for one backbone, and no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are stated. The safety-critical subset is identified by an approximate probe-based signal; the paper does not show that the selected neurons exclusively carry refusal behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were omitted from the directly relevant geometry-control comparison. Main ShaPO-versus-baseline safety benchmark tables and Hessian/win-rate comparisons were not cataloged as V5 results because they do not isolate whether a small selected parameter subset carries safety behavior.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few examples and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks that bypass refusal.
Whether ablating or modifying a small weight set removes safety behaviour. The study only restricts SAM perturbations to probe-selected neurons during DPO training.
Data or objective causes of shallow safety.
Training that spreads safety across response positions and its durability.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 labels are removed. Table 3 is an ablation of the study's own training method, and its ASR differences are small (about 0.5–3 points) with no uncertainty reported. It cites Qi et al. 2024 (an original source) only as motivation.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as safety bypasses.
Tests probe-identified value-vector neurons and selective geometry control, not whether specific weights or ranks exclusively carry safety behavior or whether removing them alone abolishes refusal.
Whether training data or objective causes safety to be shallow in response-token positions.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first response tokens and whether that depth holds up.

rows.measure: Average attack success rate (ASR) across four OOD safety benchmarks
rows.value: ASR consistently decreases as the ratio rises from 0.01% to 1%, reaches its minimum at Top-1%, then gradually rises beyond that point
rows.note: The text describes the trend and minimum, but does not give exact ASR values for the ratios.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selective control on the OOD average evaluation for LLaMA-3-8B
reader_labels.reason: Selective control yields lower ASR than no control, random control, and uniform control on both judges; see r16 and r17.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Selective neuron-ratio sweep on OOD benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The reported ASR minimum at Top-1% and increase beyond that ratio supports localization to a limited, selected subset, though not exclusive carriage of safety behavior; see r18.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Selective control does not consistently improve both judges relative to no control, and its MD ASR is higher; see r14 and r15.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Uniform and random controls and neuron ratios beyond Top-1%
reader_labels.reason: Random control gives only marginal OOD changes, uniform control is worse than selective control, and adding more than the selected ratio degrades ASR; see r6-r13 and r18.
